name: Magnesium

lead: Magnesium is an essential mineral involved in hundreds of enzyme reactions, including energy metabolism, muscle and nerve function and bone structure. About half of the body's magnesium is held in bone.
It is a common supplement for sleep, cramps and general bone health. The strongest evidence is for correcting a deficiency; beyond that, claims about cosmetic or structural benefit are weak.

paras: Magnesium acts as a cofactor for ATP-dependent enzymes and influences calcium handling, parathyroid hormone secretion and vitamin D activation, all of which affect bone turnover. It is also incorporated into the bone mineral surface and acts as a reservoir.

Supplements, especially magnesium oxide and citrate, can cause diarrhoea and abdominal cramping, and people with kidney impairment can accumulate it to dangerous levels. It can interact with some antibiotics and bisphosphonates. Dietary intake from nuts, seeds, legumes and greens is generally safe.
